market_scan.market_size_text: The relevant market is comminution and ore pre-treatment equipment within the broader mineral processing equipment market (~$23B/yr in 2025). Crushing, screening and grinding equipment alone is roughly $10-15B/yr worldwide, growing ~4-6%/yr, and comminution consumes ~36-50% of total mine-site energy, making it the single biggest energy consumer and the natural target for energy-saving retrofits. A microwave pre-treatment unit would sell as an add-on upstream of mills into this existing spend, plus a large opex-saving value pool: comminution electricity on a big copper concentrator is worth tens of $M/yr per site.
market_scan.target_customers_text: ICMM's Global Mining Dataset lists ~15,000 mining/processing facilities across 151 countries; the addressable subset for ore weakening is hard-rock concentrators (copper, gold, iron ore, PGM, lithium) — order of ~3,000-5,000 sites. Economic value concentrates in a few hundred large concentrators (>10 Mt/y) run by majors and mid-tiers. Large miners are reachable via OEM/EPCM channels but are conservative, capex-disciplined and slow (multi-year pilot-before-adoption cycles); medium miners are the realistic early adopters; small mines lack capex and power infrastructure for high-MW microwave units.
market_scan.players_text: Comminution equipment is supplied by a concentrated tier of global OEMs — Metso (#1 crushing, top-3 grinding), FLSmidth, Weir (Enduron HPGR), Sandvik, thyssenkrupp, CITIC — with the top 3 holding ~35% of crushing/screening and strong aftermarket lock-in. There is no established commercial supplier of microwave ore pre-treatment; the space is emerging (University of Nottingham + Teledyne e2v 'MicroHammer' with Rio Tinto at pilot scale; SELFRAG's high-voltage pulse machines are the closest commercialised analogue). Ore pre-treatment is therefore a contested white space the incumbents do not yet own.

regulation: EU Industrial Emissions Directive / Mining BREF (MIN BREF)

Specific energy consumption per tonne of ore is being adopted as a key environmental indicator for mine sites; BAT conclusions will push operators toward best-available energy-efficient comminution techniques — favours retrofit pre-treatment.
EU ETS + Energy Efficiency Directive (Art. 11 audits)

Carbon price (~EUR60-80/t CO2) and mandatory 4-yearly energy audits for large companies raise the cost of comminution electricity and force audited efficiency measures — strengthens the energy-saving sales case.
10% of EU extraction and 40% of processing to be domestic by 2030 with fast-tracked permitting — creates new EU concentrator builds where a Swiss technology supplier can position early.
Large emitting facilities (incl. big mines) must reduce baseline emissions ~4.9%/yr to 2030; comminution electrification/efficiency is a primary lever on grid-powered sites.
EMF/RF safety: CISPR 11/EN 55011 ISM limits + EU Directive 2013/35/EU

High-power microwave units must be shielded to ISM leakage limits at 915 MHz/2.45 GHz and worker EMF exposure limits — adds engineering/compliance requirements to machine design but no licensing barrier.
Major miners representing ~1/3 of the industry have committed to scope 1-2 net zero — pulls demand for step-change energy technologies beyond regulatory minimums.

technologies.name: Conventional crushing + SAG/ball milling (incumbent)
technologies.how: Multi-stage mechanical crushing followed by semi-autogenous and ball mills; breakage is indiscriminate, applied to the rock bulk rather than grain boundaries.
technologies.performance: Total circuit ~9-23 kWh/t depending on ore hardness (Bond work index ~10-20 kWh/t); comminution = ~36-50% of mine-site energy; only ~3-5% of input energy creates new surface area.
technologies.limits: Extremely inefficient; energy scales with ore competency; no mechanism to preferentially weaken ore — the hypothesis attacks exactly this inefficiency.

technologies.name: High-Pressure Grinding Rolls (HPGR)
technologies.how: Ore bed compressed between counter-rotating rolls; inter-particle crushing generates micro-cracks and a weaker, finer product feeding ball mills.
technologies.performance: ~15-20% lower direct comminution energy vs SAG circuits (e.g. ~7.6-19.3 kWh/t vs 9-23 kWh/t for SABC); ~23-25% lower opex; pilot data shows up to ~60% machine-level energy reduction vs ball milling alone.
technologies.limits: High capex, stud/roll wear, prefers dry feed, benefit is ore-dependent; still applies bulk mechanical stress rather than selective grain-boundary weakening — microwave can be complementary upstream, not a replacement.

technologies.name: High-voltage pulse pre-weakening (SELFRAG / electrodynamic fragmentation)
technologies.how: Sub-microsecond electrical discharges pass through immersed ore, generating plasma channels that fragment particles selectively along grain boundaries.
technologies.performance: Pre-weakening at ~1-3 kWh/t; JKMRC/Newcrest simulation of a gold-copper circuit indicated ~5 kWh/t circuit energy reduction and potential removal of pebble crushers + a 10 MW ball mill.
technologies.limits: Batch/low-throughput machines, requires water immersion and drying, electrode wear, limited industrial adoption at mining scale — microwave treats dry ore continuously at much higher throughput.

technologies.name: Mine-to-mill / blast optimisation (explosive pre-weakening)
technologies.how: Higher-intensity blasting and fragmentation modelling to deliver finer ROM feed, shifting size reduction from mills to cheaper explosive energy.
technologies.performance: Typically ~5-15% comminution energy reduction achievable where applicable; explosive energy ~$0.1-0.3/t vs electricity ~10-20x costlier per equivalent breakage.
technologies.limits: Diminishing returns, already adopted at most well-run sites, constrained by geotechnical/vibration limits — sets the bar a new pre-treatment must exceed.

technologies.name: Microwave pre-treatment (state of the art — the hypothesis technology)
technologies.how: High-power microwave energy selectively heats high-dielectric-loss mineral phases; differential thermal expansion generates inter- and trans-granular micro-cracks that weaken the ore before it enters crushers/mills.
technologies.performance: Nottingham/e2v pilot plant: 10-150 t/h at 10-200 kW, effective at ~0.3-3 kWh/t dose; Bond work index reduced ~3-9% (up to 30-40% in lab on amenable ores, e.g. Palabora 13.1→9.2 kWh/t in 10 s); flowsheet simulations: -9% to -24% specific comminution energy and up to +30% throughput; MicroHammer claims >20% energy reduction at 150 t/h demo, scalable to ~3,000 t/h.
technologies.limits: Benefit highly ore/mineralogy-dependent (needs microwave-absorbing vs transparent phase contrast); unproven at full commercial scale; very short exposure (<0.1-1 s) needed for favourable net energy balance; no operating commercial installation yet.

tech_baseline.why_better_text: Microwave pre-treatment attacks the weakest point of the incumbent flowsheet: mills waste ~95% of their energy because ore must be stressed as a bulk solid, while microwaves deposit energy selectively at grain boundaries where breakage is most valuable, for ~0.5-2 kWh/t input. Unlike HPGR or new mills, it is an add-on installed between primary crushing and milling — it debottlenecks existing circuits (+~30% modelled throughput) and avoids multi-hundred-$M mill expansions, which is a far easier capex decision than circuit replacement. Versus its closest novel rival (HVP/electrodynamic), it treats ore dry, continuously, and has demonstrated 10-150 t/h pilots with a credible path to mining-scale throughput (e2v/Nottingham modelled ~3,000 t/h).
key_assumptions: Comminution consumes ~36-50% of mine-site energy; the grinding mill is the largest single consumer (measured, Weir/Engeco 2021; US DOE bandwidth study: grinding ~40% of mining energy)
Microwave doses of ~0.3-1.3 kWh/t at high power density measurably weaken ore at pilot scale: A*b -7-14%, Bond work index -3-9% (measured, Nottingham pilot, 300 t processed under power)
Modelled -9% to -24% specific comminution energy and up to +30% throughput depending on ore and grind size (measured/simulated — not yet demonstrated at plant scale)
Net energy balance is favourable: ~1 kWh/t microwave input vs ~2-5 kWh/t downstream saving; requires sub-second high-power-density exposure (assumed — simulation-based, ore-dependent)

Sufficient fraction of world ores are amenable (need strong dielectric-loss contrast, e.g. sulphides/pyrite in quartz matrix); lab strength reductions range ~8-40% by ore (measured but highly variable — key risk)
